original_title: An ″α-Methylsulfone″ Transfer Agent: Synthesis and Application of γ-Ketosulfones
title: A reagent that bolts a masked enone onto any ketone
blurb: Sulfonyl hydrazide plus formaldehyde works as an α-methylsulfone transfer agent, adding one carbon to ketones to give γ-ketosulfones in a single metal-free pot. The sulfone doubles as a masked α-methylene ketone, and they carry it onward with nucleophiles and active methylene compounds to build cyclohexenones.

original_title: Outside Back Cover: Synthesis of Aminocyclopropanes by Redox‐Neutral Aminoalkylation
title: Aminocyclopropanes without spending a redox step
blurb: A redox-neutral aminoalkylation route to aminocyclopropanes, tidy enough to land the back cover art for this issue.

original_title: Umpolung Amide Synthesis with Nitrosoalkane Electrophiles: Pursuit of the Elusive N -Acyl Nitrone for Dipolar Cycloadditions
title: Finally landing the N-acyl nitrone everyone wanted but couldn't make
blurb: A diverted Umpolung Amide Synthesis forges the C-N bond straight into N-acyl nitrones, doubly acylated dipoles that stayed rare for fifty years because nobody had a clean route in. The pitch is cycloadditions with electron-rich alkenes that ordinary nitrones can't touch, assuming it holds past the first examples.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Regioselective Synthesis of Fluorescent Indazolo[2,3- a ]quinazolines and Their Photophysical Studies
title: Copper gets a one-pot route to fluorescent indazoloquinazolines
blurb: 3-aminoindazoles plus 2-bromobenzyl bromides, ligand-free copper, and the amine's own nitrogen does the N-benzylation before an Ullmann closure and aromatization finishes the ring. Runs on gram scale with decent functional group tolerance, and the payoff is that the products are fluorescent, so they bothered to run the photophysics too.

original_title: Validated Reversed-Phase HPLC-PDA Quantitation of Three Nitrosamine Impurities in Valsartan Tablets Using Selective Acidic Sample Preparation
title: An HPLC method that actually keeps valsartan out of the way while it hunts nitrosamines
blurb: Reversed-phase HPLC-PDA for NDMA, NDEA, and NDBA in valsartan tablets, with dilute formic acid sample prep chosen specifically to keep valsartan from dissolving and swamping the signal. Validated, not just demonstrated, which is the point given regulators are still chasing sartan nitrosamines years after that recall mess started.

original_title: Tangential flow filtration as a novel approach for fluorescent tracer purification and production up-scaling: cetuximab-800CW and ustekinumab-800CW as a proof-of-concept
title: Scaling up fluorescent antibody tracers with tangential flow filtration instead of the usual columns
blurb: TFF swapped in as the purification step for fluorescent tracers, tested on cetuximab-800CW and ustekinumab-800CW as proof of concept. The appeal is that it's a scale-up-friendly technique, not just a cleaner one, which matters more than purity numbers if these tracers are ever going to be made in bulk.

original_title: BEHOLD-1 and -2: phase 1/2 randomized studies evaluating the B7 homolog 4 protein-targeted antibody-drug conjugate mocertatug rezetecan in patients with solid tumors, including endometrial and ovarian cancers.
title: A B7-H4 ADC gets its phase 1/2 shakeout in endometrial and ovarian cancer
blurb: BEHOLD-1 and -2 are the randomized phase 1/2 studies for mocertatug rezetecan, an antibody-drug conjugate aimed at B7-H4, run across solid tumors including endometrial and ovarian cancer. Early-phase and randomized, so it's a dosing and signal-finding step, not a verdict.

original_title: Research Progress and Challenges in the Use of TROP2-Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugates for the Treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
title: Where TROP2 ADCs actually stand for triple-negative breast cancer
blurb: A review of TROP2-targeted antibody-drug conjugates as an option for TNBC, the subtype that has no ER, PR, or HER2 to target and historically nothing else to aim at. TROP2's appeal is that it's overexpressed across epithelial tumors and tied to invasion and metastasis, but this is a progress-and-challenges piece, not new data.
venue: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences

original_title: Cu/Rh-Carbene-Directed Highly Diastereoselective Dimerization of Cyclopropenes
title: Carbene dimerization that skips the usual head-to-head coupling entirely
blurb: Instead of two carbenes meeting face to face to make a flat olefin, these cyclopropenes under Cu or Rh go through C–H insertion then a [2+1] cycloaddition, landing on cyclopropa-fused indanes with excellent diastereoselectivity. DFT pins the selectivity on π–π stacking steering the approach, which is a cleaner mechanistic story than most dimerizations get.

original_title: Diastereo- and Regioselective Assembly of Furan-Fused Piperidine Frameworks via Rhodium-Catalyzed Intramolecular Carbonyl Ylide Cycloaddition
title: Rhodium carbonyl ylides build furan-fused piperidines with the stereochemistry under control
blurb: N-allylated amino aldehydes and diallyl diazo compounds feed a rhodium-catalyzed intramolecular carbonyl ylide cycloaddition, closing furano-fused piperidine and piperidinone scaffolds with both diastereo- and regiocontrol. A fairly specific ring system, but getting both selectivities at once from an intramolecular ylide cycloaddition isn't nothing.

original_title: Stereodivergent Synthesis of C -Glycosides from Glycals by Ni-Catalyzed Cross-Hydrocarbonylation of Alkenes
title: Nickel finally gives C-glycosides a stereodivergent route from glycals
blurb: C-glycosides beat their O- and N-linked cousins on pharmacokinetics but have been a pain to make with real stereocontrol from cheap starting material. This nickel-catalyzed iterative hydrocarbonylation of glycals with alkenes gets stereodivergent C-acylated glycosides, meaning you can pick your stereochemistry rather than take whatever the substrate hands you.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Carbon dioxide as a multifunctional regulator in electrochemical vicinal bromination
title: CO2 pulls triple duty in an electrochemical vicinal bromination
blurb: Vicinal dibromides are everywhere in bioactive molecules, but cheap, practical ways to make them electrochemically still struggle, especially with N–H substrates that misbehave under oxidative conditions. Here CO2 isn't just along for the ride, it's doing multiple regulatory jobs in the reaction, which is the actual hook of a method that otherwise sounds like a bromination paper.

original_title: Aza-Berson–Willcott Rearrangement
title: The Berson-Willcott rearrangement finally gets a nitrogen version
blurb: The original Berson-Willcott rearrangement has sat stuck in all-carbon systems for decades, slowed by harsh conditions and reversible equilibria. The aza version here breaks that constraint and builds cyclopropane-fused quinolines with full regio- and diastereocontrol under mild conditions, and DFT turns up a noncanonical mechanism nobody was expecting for a ring expansion like this.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Asymmetric enzymatic hydrophosphorylation through O 2 activation
title: An enzyme that builds carbon-phosphorus bonds, which nature almost never does
blurb: A repurposed flavin enzyme turns O2-derived reactive oxygen species into phosphorus-centered radicals, then closes the loop with radical addition and enzymatic hydrogen atom transfer, enantioselectively. Enzymatic C-P bond formation is rare enough on its own to be the news here, and the fact it tolerates a range of P-H donors is what would make it an actual route to chiral organophosphorus compounds instead of a one-substrate demo.

original_title: Visible Light‐Induced [2 + 2]‐Cycloaddition and Photo‐Ene Reactions: Spin‐Dependent Catalysis and Quantum Tunneling Effects
title: Why the same photocatalyst gives you a cycloaddition or a photo-ene product
blurb: Energy-transfer catalysis with ITX funnels excitation through a 1ππ*→3nπ*→3ππ* cascade, and Marcus theory plus ab initio calculations show the spin state reached along that path is what actually decides whether you get [2+2] cycloaddition or a photo-ene reaction. More mechanistic accounting than new chemistry, but it puts a real explanation behind a chemoselectivity problem that's mostly been hand-waved.

original_title: Varying Mechanisms Dominate Formate Formation in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction on Cu, Au, and Pb: A Constant Potential DFT-Based Microkinetic Analysis
title: Cu, Au, and Pb make formate from CO2 by different mechanisms entirely
blurb: A constant-potential DFT microkinetic analysis finds that electrochemical CO2-to-formate doesn't run through one debated pathway, it runs through a different dominant mechanism on each of copper, gold, and lead. Mostly useful as a corrective to catalyst-design papers that have been arguing over a single universal mechanism that apparently isn't one.

original_title: Quinoline-Based Amide Foldamers with One-Handed Chirality Induced by an Asymmetric Plane
title: A planar-chiral cyclophane forces a quinoline foldamer to pick one helix and keep it
blurb: Bolt a planar-chiral [2.2]paracyclophane unit onto a quinoline foldamer and the R or S plane locks in the P or M helical sense every time, confirmed by X-ray and CD. The trimers come out as a separable racemic pair of single-handed helices rather than an uncontrolled mix, which is the actual point if you ever wanted a foldamer with predictable handedness.

original_title: Predictive Model for Acid-Catalyzed SN1 Solvolysis Racemization of Chiral Alcohols in Water
title: A cheat sheet for whether your chiral alcohol will racemize in water
blurb: A linear regression model predicts the activation energy for acid-catalyzed SN1 racemization of chiral alcohols straight from the calculated electronic energy gap to the carbocation intermediate. It's a screening tool for med chem rather than a mechanistic finding, but that's exactly what you want before scaling up a stereocenter that won't hold.

original_title: Hydrogen Bond Network Descriptors Dictate Reactivity and Selectivity of CO2 Electroreduction
title: Tuning water's hydrogen-bond network to steer CO2 electroreduction
blurb: Dosing the electrolyte with different urea derivatives lets the authors independently dial two descriptors, hydrogen bond strength and hydrogen bond number, and both turn out to predict CO2RR reactivity and selectivity. A knob that isn't the catalyst itself, which is usually just lumped into "the electrolyte" and ignored.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photobiocatalytic Linear Deracemization of β‐Hydroxynitriles
title: Deracemizing β-hydroxynitriles by splitting them apart and reducing them back together
blurb: Step one is TBADT photooxidizing the racemic alcohol under 390 nm light, step two is an alcohol dehydrogenase reducing it back asymmetrically, giving a linear deracemization instead of the 50% ceiling a kinetic resolution would hit. Getting a photocatalytic oxidation and a biocatalytic reduction to tolerate the same pot, even run sequentially, is usually what kills cascades like this, so that's the actual achievement.

original_title: Asymmetric Access to Spirobenzofuran Oxindoles via Organocascade Reaction of Unprotected 3-Chlorooxindoles with 2-Hydroxy-β-Nitrostyrenes
title: Building spirobenzofuran oxindoles without protecting groups first
blurb: An organocascade reaction runs directly on unprotected 3-chlorooxindoles, forming a new C-C bond, a new C-O bond, and two stereocenters in one pot, enantioselectively. They back it up with gram-scale and stereodivergent runs that don't cost yield or selectivity, plus HRMS titrations supporting the proposed mechanism, so this one did its homework.

original_title: Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex Catalysis in Synthetic Chemistry
title: Turning electron donor-acceptor photochemistry from a stoichiometric trick into real catalysis
blurb: A review on electron donor-acceptor complexes, long familiar as stoichiometric radical photochemistry but only recently pushed into actual catalytic cycles, where the hard part is coupling charge-transfer excitation to catalyst regeneration instead of just burning through reagent. It's a map of the design principles that make that turnover work, not a new result, but the field needed the map.

original_title: B−H oxidation enables modular synthesis of vicinally trifunctionalized boron-rich clusters
title: Oxidizing a B-H bond to open up boron clusters for modular functionalization
blurb: B-H oxidation serves as the handle for installing three different substituents at adjacent positions on boron-rich clusters. Thin on detail beyond that, but a clean-sounding modular route if it extends past the reported cases.

original_title: A stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for quantification of impurities in sertraline hydrochloride finished dosage forms using quality by design with environmental assessment
title: A greener HPLC method for sertraline's impurities
blurb: An AQbD-designed, stability-indicating RP-HPLC-UV method for quantifying impurities in sertraline hydrochloride tablets, built with an environmental-performance angle alongside the usual validation work. Solid regulatory housekeeping rather than a breakthrough, but someone has to keep the impurity limits honest.

original_title: From absolute barriers to responsiveness: How London dispersion modulates kinetic-thermodynamic relationships
title: London dispersion as a thermostat for reaction barriers
blurb: The claim is that dispersion forces shift how a reaction's barrier tracks its thermodynamics, turning what looks like a fixed barrier into something more tunable across a series. Barely anything to go on here beyond that framing, so take it as a headline, not a result.

original_title: Improved Photocatalysis in Diisocyanide-Supported Heteroleptic Four-Coordinate Copper(I) β-Diketiminate Complexes
title: Diisocyanide ligands give Cu(I) photocatalysts a longer excited-state life
blurb: New heteroleptic four-coordinate Cu(I) beta-diketiminate complexes carry chelating diisocyanide ligands, one built on a m-terphenyl core, chasing the usual photoredox wishlist: strong visible absorption, long-lived excited states, and real redox punch. The pitch is an earth-abundant stand-in for iridium and ruthenium photocatalysts, worth it if the numbers hold up outside this paper.

original_title: Electrochemical Oxidative Dearomatization of Indole with Carboxylic Acid via 1,2-Acyloxy Migration for the Synthesis of C2-Quaternary Indolin-3-ones
title: Making indole's C2 quaternary, electrochemically
blurb: A KBr-promoted electrochemical setup pushes indoles and carboxylic acids through a 1,2-acyloxy migration to build C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones, with water supplying the oxygen atom instead of a metal oxidant. No metal, no stoichiometric oxidant, and isotope labeling backs the proposed esterification-then-migration mechanism, which is the part that actually distinguishes this from the usual indole dearomatization.

original_title: Bimetallic Aluminum Hydride s-Block (Li, Na, K) Compounds in Catalytic Hydroboration
title: Swapping transition metals for alkali-doped aluminum hydrides in hydroboration
blurb: Bimetallic aluminum hydride ate complexes paired with Li, Na, or K hydroborate carbonyls more actively than plain aluminum hydride, with the alkali metal apparently doing real cooperative work rather than just sitting there. Even the authors admit the identity of the active species in carbonyl hydroboration is still up for debate, so the mechanism is the loose end here.

original_title: CAN-Promoted Boc2O-Mediated Cascade Conversion of Aziridines to Oxazolidinones
title: Turning aziridines into oxazolidinones without touching CO2
blurb: CAN promotes a Boc2O-mediated cascade that opens aziridines and cyclizes them into oxazolidinones, with Boc2O standing in for CO2 as the carbonyl source under mild, CO2-free conditions. Forty-six examples spanning 16-99% yield, so plenty of substrates where it clearly struggles, but gram-scale runs suggest it's not just a paper reaction.

original_title: Integrating Fragment Screening and Covalent Chemistry to Drug DNA-Binding Proteins: RAD52 as a Case Study
title: Hitting RAD52's DNA-binding groove with covalent fragments
blurb: Protein-DNA interfaces are usually too flat, polar, and solvent-exposed to drug, so this combines fragment screening for DNA-mimetic binders with covalent capture of a nearby nucleophile, using RAD52's ssDNA-binding groove as the proving ground. An X-ray fragment screen turned up carboxylate fragments that recapitulate the native DNA contacts, early days, but a real strategy for a target class usually written off as hopeless.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sterling Pharma Solutions doubles ADC manufacturing capacity at Deeside with new GMP suite - Manufacturing Chemist
title: Sterling Pharma doubles down on ADC manufacturing at Deeside
blurb: A new GMP suite doubles Sterling Pharma Solutions' ADC manufacturing capacity at Deeside. Thin on detail, but another CDMO betting that ADC demand keeps outrunning capacity rather than catching up to it.

original_title: Modular Cyano-fluoroalkylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by Photoinduced Fe-LMCT Catalysis
title: Iron photocatalysis turns TFA into a fluoroalkyl radical source
blurb: Fe-LMCT photocatalysis pairs cheap trifluoroacetic acid, and its relatives, as the fluoroalkyl source with tosyl cyanide as a low-toxicity cyanating agent, adding both across unactivated alkenes in one redox-neutral step. Forty examples up to 83% yield, including biologically relevant substrates, and the resulting beta-fluoroalkylated nitriles look like genuinely useful handles for further derivatization rather than dead-end products.

original_title: Cyano-Engineered Tetraphenylethene-Based Pd2L4 Metallacages for Iodide Detection
title: Pd2L4 cages built to grab iodide
blurb: Tetraphenylethene-based Pd2L4 metallacages with cyano-vinylene spacers create an inward-facing, electron-poor cavity tuned for iodide, an anion that's normally awkward to recognize given its size and weak hydration. Both cages are also AIE-active, so binding should show up as a change in luminescence rather than needing separate spectroscopy to confirm it.

original_title: Tartrate-Assisted Hydrothermal Calcination Strategy for Compositionally Tunable Doped ZnO: Synthesis and Representative OER Evaluation
title: A tartrate shortcut to dial-a-dopant ZnO
blurb: Toss Zn and a dopant metal into tartrate under hydrothermal conditions, calcine, and out comes doped ZnO, with Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu all demonstrated as drop-in dopants. The OER numbers are billed as "representative," so this reads like a synthesis platform paper more than a best-in-class catalyst claim.

original_title: Long‐Range Atomic Periodicity Unlocks Durable Water Electrolysis
title: Ordering the atoms in an Ir-V catalyst so the iridium stops dissolving
blurb: Iridium OER catalysts are good but leach themselves to death in acidic PEM electrolyzers. Building a long-range ordered Ir-V intermetallic with strong Ir-V bonding instead of a disordered alloy keeps the structure intact and suppresses that dissolution, backed by both theory and experiment.

original_title: Interfacial Electric Fields in Water Nanodroplets Are Weakly Dependent on Curvature and pH
title: The electric field at a water droplet's surface barely cares how curved it is
blurb: Microdroplet chemistry runs weirdly fast, and the interfacial electric field gets blamed for it a lot. Full quantum-level mapping (deep learning MD plus ab initio resampling) across flat interfaces and droplets of different sizes and charge states finds a steady ~1.0-1.2 V/Å field regardless of curvature or pH. If the field itself barely moves with curvature, curvature-driven field enhancement isn't the explanation for why microdroplets react the way they do.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Solvent-mediated electrochemical acetylene semihydrogenation for continuous production of polymer-grade ethylene
title: Running acetylene semihydrogenation as a continuous electrochemical process
blurb: An electrochemical, solvent-mediated route that semihydrogenates acetylene straight into polymer-grade ethylene as a continuous process, rather than the usual batch thermal catalytic step.

original_title: Oxygen-tolerant green-light photopolymerizations with type I boron-alkylated BODIPYs: The power of a methylene
title: One methylene group turns on oxygen-tolerant photopolymerization
blurb: A boron-alkylated BODIPY type I photoinitiator that keeps curing in air, with the effect apparently hinging on a single methylene group in the structure. Thin on detail beyond that, but a neat reminder of how small a tweak decides oxygen tolerance.

original_title: Benzoxaborole-Inspired p K a-Guided Search for a Borine Alternative Uncovers a Borylurea Scaffold with Unique Properties and Reactivity
title: Chasing benzoxaborole's pKa trick turns up a borylurea instead
blurb: Benzoxaboroles work as drugs partly because of their neutral pKa, but nobody's managed to repeat that trick with other B-OH heterocycles. Screening upward of 15 non-aromatic and pseudo-aromatic six-membered borine analogs for the right pKa profile didn't produce a better benzoxaborole, it turned up an unrelated borylurea scaffold with its own distinct reactivity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Spin Polarization Enables Spin-Conserved Intermediate Migration for Selective C–N Coupling toward Urea Electrosynthesis
title: Spin-polarizing iron to stop urea electrosynthesis from leaking nitrogen to ammonia
blurb: Co-reducing CO2 and nitrate to urea keeps losing the race to C-N coupling, with ammonia forming instead. Subbing Cu into FeSe2 shifts Fe's electronic configuration into spin-polarized centers, and the resulting mixed-valence Fe species is what they credit for letting the key intermediate migrate without a spin flip, which is the step behind the better C-N coupling.

original_title: Targeting the TRA-1-60 Glycoepitope Enables Selective ImmunoPET Imaging of Ovarian Cancer.
title: Imaging ovarian cancer through a stem-cell marker it has no business wearing
blurb: TRA-1-60 is normally a pluripotency glycoepitope, not something you'd expect on a solid tumor, but targeting it apparently gives selective immunoPET imaging of ovarian cancer. Still a bioRxiv preprint, so no peer review yet on how selective "selective" really is.

original_title: Active synthesizability prediction for a virtual space of 395 million catalyst candidates with small data
title: Predicting which of 395 million catalyst candidates are even worth making
blurb: NHC precatalysts built from pyridine[1,5]imidazolium salts are handy once you have them, but not all of them are easy to actually synthesize. Starting from real attempts on 127 compounds, they set up a feedback loop where a supervised ML model keeps updating its synthesizability estimates, then ran it across a virtual library of 395 million candidates. Small-data active learning doing triage before anyone wastes a flask.

original_title: Structure-Dependent Effects of Lipid Conjugation on Cytosolic Accumulation in Escherichia coli and Mammalian Cells
title: The same lipid tail gets you into a HeLa cell and locked out of E. coli
blurb: Their CHAMP assay measures actual cytosolic accumulation rather than just membrane binding, and running a lipid-conjugate library through both HeLa and E. coli turns up opposite trends: most lipid tails that help a payload reach mammalian cytosol end up hurting accumulation in E. coli. Bad news for assuming a lipidation trick that works in human cells will carry over to Gram-negative bacteria.

original_title: Efficient Photocatalytic H2O2 Formation by a Porphyrin-TiO2 Hybrid Catalyst in Pure Water
title: A porphyrin-TiO2 hybrid that makes H2O2 from nothing but light and water
blurb: Bolting a carboxylated dodecaphenylporphyrin onto TiO2 gives a hybrid photocatalyst that produces hydrogen peroxide in ultrapure water under illumination, no sacrificial donors or solvent tricks needed. Useful if H2O2 is really going to be treated as an energy carrier, though the actual efficiency numbers are the part that'll decide if this beats the usual systems.

original_title: Intramolecular Direct Arylation Enables Access to Diverse Photophysical Properties for π‐Expanded 1,4‐Dihydropyrrolo[3,2‐ b ]pyrroles
title: One arylation twice over gets you a whole family of DHPP dyes
blurb: A double intramolecular direct arylation builds out dihydropyrrolopyrrole dyes with up to 20 fused aromatic rings, some helically twisted, each with its own fluorescence and optical profile. One modular route, a spread of photophysics on the other end.

original_title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
title: A two-step fix for the oxetane bioisostere nobody could access modularly
blurb: 3,3-diaryloxetanes are a handy ketone stand-in for drug discovery but hard to build flexibly. Here aryllithium addition to 3-oxetanone and alkoxide trapping gives a stable tetrafluoropyridyl ether intermediate, which then undergoes Ni-catalyzed cross-coupling with aryl boronates to install the second ring. Two steps, and the substitution pattern is basically whatever boronate you have on the shelf.

original_title: High-Affinity Y1 Receptor Theranostics: First-in-Class Stabilized Nonapeptides for Breast Cancer Imaging and Therapy
title: A stiffer, tighter-binding peptide for Y1 receptor breast cancer theranostics
blurb: Starting from the Y1R antagonist [Lys2,Arg4]BVD-15, these stabilized nonapeptides radiolabel at over 95% purity and bind the receptor up to 60-fold tighter than the parent compound. Y1R overexpression spans multiple stages of breast cancer, so a tighter-binding theranostic pair is the point here, this is still binding-affinity data, not an imaged patient.

original_title: First Radioligand Therapy Approved for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer - Cleveland Clinic
title: Radioligand therapy finally approved for hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer
blurb: The approval moves radioligand therapy up a line, into metastatic disease that's still hormone-sensitive rather than waiting for castration-resistance to set in. First clearance of its kind at that earlier stage.

original_title: Differentiation of axial spondyloarthritis-related lesions from degenerative lesions on Na[18F]Fluoride PET/CT in a longitudinal dataset of patients with radiographic axial spondyloarthritis
title: Trying to tell spondyloarthritis lesions apart from plain old wear and tear on bone PET
blurb: Twenty patients with radiographic axial spondyloarthritis got Na-18F PET/CT before biologic therapy and again at 12 and 52 weeks, with blinded readers scoring each lesion as disease-related or just degenerative. The longitudinal angle is the point, seeing whether uptake patterns actually separate the two over a year of treatment instead of just flagging every hot spot as spine inflammation. Small cohort, so call it a first pass at the distinction.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Lost in Overlap: Mapping Local Composition Landscapes to Predict the Upper Measurable Mass Limit of Copolymers and Terpolymers by MALDI-TOF MS
title: Mapping exactly where copolymer MALDI spectra stop being trustworthy
blurb: Push copolymer MALDI-TOF to higher molecular weights and the peaks start overlapping because too many compositions and isotope patterns land on the same mass. This maps which species actually contribute to a given peak and uses that to predict the upper mass limit where the technique quietly stops working, rather than leaving you to squint at a crowded spectrum and guess.

original_title: Acanthamoeba ATP synthase structure reveals the TCA cycle is tethered to OXPHOS
title: Catching the TCA cycle physically wired into the ATP synthase
blurb: Cryo-EM run straight on unenriched Acanthamoeba mitochondrial lysate, backed by MS proteomics, resolved ATP synthase, Hsp60, and complex III without purifying any of them first. The ATP synthase shows up in an IF1-inhibited state, and the structure argues the TCA cycle is physically tethered to OXPHOS rather than just passing metabolites through solution, worked out in an organism most people only know as an eye infection.

original_title: Integrating Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Data with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Protein Complex Structure Prediction
title: Letting ion mobility data veto AlphaFold's worse guesses at protein complexes
blurb: AlphaFold handles single proteins fine but gets shaky on complexes, so this docks AlphaFold-predicted subunits with Rosetta and then filters the resulting models against collision cross sections from ion mobility MS, using a new scoring function built for that comparison. IM-MS alone gives you no atomic detail, but apparently enough shape information to tell which docked model is wrong.

original_title: Directed Electrocatalytic Nitrate Conversion via H-Bond Network Fortification
title: Steering nitrate electroreduction by fortifying the electrolyte's hydrogen bonds, not the catalyst
blurb: Selectivity in nitrate reduction usually gets chased through catalyst design, but here it's the electrolyte doing the work: dosing in oxalic acid or acetic acid reshapes the interfacial hydrogen-bond network and redirects proton transfer, steering which nitrogen product comes out. Two simple, differently shaped additives, apparently enough to flip selectivity without touching the catalyst.

original_title: HFIP-promoted Lewis acid-free one-pot synthesis of pyran derivatives under mild conditions
title: A pyran synthesis that skips the Lewis acid entirely
blurb: HFIP alone, acting as both solvent and promoter, pushes a three-component aldehyde/malononitrile/dimedone coupling to 92% yield in just 5 minutes at 55°C. Swap in ethyl acetoacetate and you get the amino-cyanopyran analogs instead. No metal catalyst needed, just the fluorinated alcohol doing double duty.

original_title: Synthesis of E -Thiovinylphosphonates via Visible-Light Mediated One-Step C–S and C–P Bond Formation Reaction
title: Light builds the C-S and C-P bonds in one go
blurb: A three-component reaction of thiols, alkynes, and phosphites under visible light gives E-thiovinylphosphonates in up to 90% yield with solid regio- and stereocontrol. Forming a C(sp2)-S and a C(sp2)-P bond in the same step is the genuinely rare part; the starting materials are the boring, already-on-the-shelf kind.

original_title: Hydantoin Impurity Formation During Peptide N-Terminal Acetylation with Acetic Anhydride
title: Your N-terminal acetylation might be quietly making hydantoins
blurb: Standard Ac2O acetylation of peptide N-termini turns out to spawn hydantoin and N-acetyl hydantoin byproducts nobody had flagged before, now pinned down by HRMS and NMR. Isotope labeling clears the acetic anhydride of supplying the extra carbonyl and points at the solvent instead, and formation is solvent- and sequence-dependent enough that avoiding it is just a matter of picking better conditions.

original_title: A triple carbonylation cascade converts aldehydes into threofuranoses
title: Aldehydes to sugars in one carbonylation cascade
blurb: A rhodium-catalyzed triple carbonylation takes plain aldehydes straight to defined 4-carbothreofuranoses in a single pot, something iterative carbonylation chemistry has struggled with for a while. If the substrate scope holds up, it's a genuinely modular route into oxygen-rich sugar scaffolds.

original_title: A Proximity Hierarchical Template Adhesion Reaction for Tripartite Profiling of Glycosylation-Associated Biomolecular Information
title: Untangling which glycosylation signal you're actually looking at
blurb: Proximity imaging of cell-surface glycosylation usually hands back one blended signal. This PH-TAR method splits it into three independent readouts instead: surface glycans, total biomolecules, and the glycosylation-associated subset, rather than lumping them together.

original_title: Oxidation State Effects on Decoherence in Isovalent 4f7 Complexes
title: Zero-field splitting as a snitch on oxidation state
blurb: Pulsed EPR at W-band on isovalent Eu2+/Gd3+/Tb4+ complexes, including the first such measurement on a molecular Tb4+, finds phase memory times at 5K drop as zero-field splitting grows. ZFS isn't just tracking distortion from cubic symmetry here, it's also picking up the electronic structure changes oxidation causes underneath a seemingly similar 4f7 shell.

original_title: Value of Dual-Time-Point [ 18 F]Fluorocholine PET/CT for Challenging Preoperative Parathyroid Imaging
title: A second-timepoint fix for tricky parathyroid scans
blurb: Dual-time-point F-18-fluorocholine PET/CT aimed at the preoperative parathyroid localization cases that are otherwise hard to pin down.

original_title: Laser-Induced Graphene Microarrays for Enhanced Quantitative Precision in Surface-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry
title: Graphene microarrays going after SALDI's precision problem
blurb: Laser desorption MS is great for salty, scarce biological samples, but shot-to-shot variation from uneven laser-sample contact has long muddied the quantitation. A laser-induced graphene microarray format is built to even that out, chasing the reproducibility SALDI has been missing for quantitative work.

original_title: Ultrafast Aqueous Photoinduced Electron/Energy Transfer Reversible Addition–Fragmentation Chain Transfer Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly: Wavelength-Dependent Morphologies and Scalable Nanoparticle Preparation
title: An orange-light PET-RAFT system that actually moves fast
blurb: PET-RAFT polymerization-induced self-assembly keeps its oxygen tolerance but usually crawls. A naphthyloxy-Z aryloxy xanthate chain transfer agent under orange light hits a propagation rate of 0.89/min and clears 80% monomer conversion quickly, with particle morphology shifting depending on the wavelength used. Fast and apparently scalable, if the morphology control is as tunable as it sounds.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Tale of Two Heterocycles: How Oxygen and Sulfur Shape Divergent Kemp Reactivity
title: Swap the oxygen for sulfur and the Kemp elimination changes its tune
blurb: Benzisoxazoles run Kemp elimination through a clean, concerted path with no detectable intermediate. Benzisothiazoles, the sulfur analog nobody had bothered characterizing, turn out to do it too, and this is the first look at what their reaction product actually is.

original_title: Single cell multi-omics guided hydrogel enables closed-loop therapy for renal osteodystrophy.
title: A hydrogel that reads single-cell data to treat kidney bone disease
blurb: Single-cell multi-omics used to steer a closed-loop hydrogel for renal osteodystrophy, the bone disease that comes with chronic kidney failure. Light on details beyond that, but pairing an omics readout with an automated delivery loop is the actual idea worth watching.

original_title: Choosing right distillation bridge size
title: Choosing right distillation bridge size
blurb: After years of multiple columns a day I found myself in a position where distillation becomes more viable due to my scale and the volatility of my compounds. In contrast to the column diameter/silica loading I have no idea about the different distillation bridge and optional vigreux column size, right now it is gut feeling alone. At what scale or BP difference do I choose eg. a shortpath/microstill/a vigreux column, when larger ones. And when should I use Claisen type bridges over the normal ones. Asking around in other labs and a search on google didn´t give me satisfying answers/rules of thu

original_title: What protocol do you use for synthesizing thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acids from L-cysteine HCl and substituted benzaldehydes?
title: What protocol do you use for synthesizing thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acids from L-cysteine HCl and substituted benzaldehydes?
blurb: Hi everyone, I’m working on the synthesis of thiazolidine-4-carboxylic acid derivatives from L-cysteine hydrochloride and substituted benzaldehydes, and I’d really like to hear what protocols people have actually found to work well in the lab. I’ve found several literature procedures for this reaction, but the conditions vary quite a bit in terms of the solvent system, concentration, amount of base, temperature and reaction time. I’m currently trying L-cysteine hydrochloride with NaHCO₃ in water and dissolving the substituted benzaldehyde separately in methanol/ethanol before combining them. I

original_title: Bioorthogonal chemistries for theranostics and radioconjugates.
title: A review of bioorthogonal chemistry for radioconjugates
blurb: A round-up of click-type bioorthogonal reactions as they get used in theranostics and radioconjugate construction. No new data, just the field collected in one place.

original_title: Facile Gram-Scale Solution Phase Synthesis of a Universal Cathepsin B-Cleavable Antibody-Drug Conjugate Linker
title: Scaling up the ADC linker everyone already relies on
blurb: A gram-scale, solution-phase route to the Glu-Val-Cit cathepsin B-cleavable linker, the one cut by both mouse and human cathepsin B, with the PABOH self-immolative spacer attached for free-drug release. Not a new linker, just a practical way to make a lot of the one people already use.

original_title: Methods for inferring interaction potentials from cross-linking mass spectrometry data.
title: Pulling interaction potentials out of cross-linking MS data
blurb: Methods for inferring interaction potentials from cross-linking mass spectrometry data, landing in a physics journal rather than a structural biology one.

original_title: [(89)Zr]Zr-DFO-EPO Imaging of Ischemia-Induced Cellular Stress.
title: Zr-89-DFO-EPO as a tracer for stressed, ischemic cells
blurb: PET imaging with Zr-89 chelated to DFO-tagged erythropoietin, used to visualize ischemia-induced cellular stress directly rather than infer it after the fact.

original_title: DBCO/Azide-Appended Thioesters Enable Proximal-Dependent Cysteine to Lysine Labeling through S → N Acyl Shift
title: A thioester trick that hands a label from cysteine to a nearby lysine
blurb: DBCO- and azide-tagged thioesters first grab free cysteine thiols, then an S→N acyl shift moves the tag onto a neighboring lysine, giving proximity-dependent labeling instead of random cysteine tagging.

original_title: cGMP production of radiometal solutions from solid targets at a university-scale facility
title: cGMP radiometals without a commercial-scale buildout
blurb: cGMP-grade production of radiometal solutions from solid targets, run at university scale rather than in an industrial facility. The point is that you don't need the industrial footprint to hit cGMP.

original_title: Electrochemical evaluation of Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox behavior and coordination stability in copper radiopharmaceuticals: recent progress
title: Copper radiopharma's redox headache, reviewed
blurb: Cu-64 and Cu-67 look good on paper for theranostic pairs, decent half-life and emissions, but Cu(II) and Cu(I) want different donor geometries, so the metal keeps trying to slip its chelator. This review tracks where that stability fight currently stands.

original_title: Functional Nucleic Acid-Antibody Conjugates for Effective Tumor Targeted Therapy With Controllable Side Effects.
title: Antibody conjugates with a nucleic acid payload and a side-effect dial
blurb: Antibody conjugates carrying functional nucleic acid cargo for tumor-targeted therapy, pitched specifically on keeping side effects controllable rather than just improving targeting.

original_title: A Practical Palladium-Catalyzed Cysteine Arylation Platform for Late-Stage Functionalization of Peptides and Proteins
title: Cysteine arylation that runs in a beaker of buffer at body temperature
blurb: Palladium-catalyzed, site-selective cysteine arylation using aryl thianthrenium salts with a RuPhos-Pd-G3 catalyst, in aqueous buffer at 37°C, no added base, photoinitiator, or organic cosolvent. Mild enough to run directly on peptides and proteins instead of just model compounds.

original_title: A dual-crosslinked silk fibroin hydrogel with aldehyde-functionalized glycyrrhizic acid as a structural-pharmacological crosslinker for diabetic wound healing.
title: A wound hydrogel where the crosslinker doubles as the drug
blurb: A dual-crosslinked silk fibroin hydrogel using aldehyde-functionalized glycyrrhizic acid as both structural crosslinker and pharmacological agent, aimed at diabetic wound healing.

original_title: A modular framework for antibody–drug conjugate biomarkers - Nature
title: A shared playbook for ADC biomarkers
blurb: A modular framework meant to standardize how biomarkers get built and validated for antibody-drug conjugates, so programs stop building their own panel from scratch every time. No data to judge it on here, just the framework itself.

original_title: De Novo Design of a TROP-2-Targeting Peptide PET Tracer via AI-Guided Binding Interface Mimicry
title: An AI-designed peptide that images TROP-2 without a biopsy
blurb: PepMimic designed a peptide, TR23, from scratch by mimicking a known binding interface rather than screening for one. Tagged with DOTA and 68Ga for PET, it binds TROP-2 at nanomolar affinity (26.8 nM) as a tracer meant to replace immunohistochemistry on biopsied tissue. Still a probe at the binding-data stage, but the whole appeal is skipping the biopsy.

original_title: Beyond Inhibition: Targeted Degradation of NLRP3 by Autophagy-Tethering Bifunctional Compounds as a Therapy for Inflammatory Bowel Disease
title: Degrading NLRP3 instead of just blocking it, for IBD
blurb: Starting from their own NLRP3 inhibitor LD5, which happens to also bind LC3, they built bivalent ATTECs that hijack autophagy to destroy NLRP3 rather than sit on it; M3 came out the most potent degrader. The actual point of the paper is justifying why you'd bother degrading a target you already have a working inhibitor for, using their own head-to-head comparisons to make that case.

original_title: A Science-Based Proposal for the Identification Threshold of Organic Impurities in Drug–Linker Intermediates Used to Produce Antibody–Drug Conjugates
title: Putting a number on how much ADC drug-linker impurity is too much to ignore
blurb: The field never pinned down when a drug-linker impurity in antibody-drug conjugates needs full identification rather than just tracking. They propose 0.25% w/w, a quarter of the existing 1.0% qualification threshold, backed by four separate safety criteria including a 200-fold margin under ICH Q3A limits, checked against 47 clinical-stage ADCs. Dry regulatory math, but the kind that decides what actually gets characterized.

original_title: Photocrosslinkable and ultrasound-responsive composite hydrogels for osteoporotic bone defect repair.
title: A hydrogel set by light, triggered afterward by ultrasound, for brittle bone
blurb: A composite hydrogel for osteoporotic bone defects that's photocrosslinked into place and then ultrasound-responsive. That's as much as there is to go on.

original_title: Proteome-guided drug discovery maps and mitigates therapeutic degrader toxicity
title: Mapping why protein degraders turn toxic, before it happens in patients
blurb: Systematic proteomic profiling of degrader drugs to find the actual mechanisms driving their toxicity, then using that map to design safer, more effective degraders for prostate cancer. The useful part is the mitigation, not just cataloguing what goes wrong.

original_title: Impact of Ring Topology in Thioether-Containing Polyazamacrocycles on the Chelation of the Auger Electron Emitter Mercury-197m/g
title: Ring shape doesn't matter for grabbing mercury-197m/g, until you check the thermodynamics
blurb: Four thioether macrocycles with different ring topologies all bind Hg2+ at the same speed at room temperature, so kinetics is a wash. How tightly they hold on afterward, though, depends heavily on backbone and donor set, which is the part that actually matters for keeping an Auger emitter put in a tumor.

original_title: Aziridination-Based Crosslinking Enables Site-Resolved Elucidation of Lipid Binding and Protein Conformational Changes
title: Snapshotting where lipids actually touch proteins, with an aziridine
blurb: Azi-LPXL-MS installs an aziridine onto the unsaturated acyl chains of native lipids, then crosslinks it to nearby lysines so mass spec can resolve exactly where a lipid sits on a protein and what shifts when it binds. A chemoselective fix for lipid-protein contacts that are usually too transient to pin down site by site.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Deciphering the Structure−Activity Relationships Underpinning the Linkerology of Bivalent EGFR Inhibitors
title: What actually makes a linker work in bivalent EGFR inhibitors
blurb: A systematic SAR study of the linkers connecting ATP-allosteric bivalent EGFR inhibitors, molecules that bridge two adjacent binding sites for outsized potency gains. The payoff is identifying which linker design choices actually drive that gain versus which just add bulk.

original_title: [ 89 Zr]Zr-DFO-EPO Imaging of Ischemia-Induced Cellular Stress
title: Imaging ischemic stress with a zirconium-tagged EPO tracer
blurb: A [89Zr]Zr-DFO-EPO PET tracer aimed at picking up cellular stress from ischemia directly, rather than inferring it from downstream damage. Light on detail beyond that, straight out of the Journal of Nuclear Medicine.

original_title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
title: Simulating how a polymer tether actually sits on a protein
blurb: An enhanced-sampling MD framework built specifically to characterize protein-polymer bioconjugate interfaces. The point is that conjugation isn't free: strong polymer-protein interactions can boost stability and affinity but also distort the native structure, and this is aimed at pinning down that tradeoff rather than assuming it away.

original_title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
title: A chemiluminescent probe that needs two separate 'yes' signals before it lights up
blurb: CLTZ probes link a tetrazine bioorthogonal trigger to a dioxetane chemiluminophore through a vinylene linker, so light only turns on when both a cancer biomarker and the bioorthogonal reaction are present. Chemiluminescence's low background finally put to use in this dual-locked setup, aimed at a urine test rather than another injectable dye.

original_title: De novo protein design in an expanded chemical space
title: Protein design that isn't stuck with the usual 20 amino acids
blurb: CheMoDesign takes a pretrained all-atom structure model, loosens its pair-representation conditioning while keeping the chemical anchors, then denoises sequences back around user-specified chemistry, PTMs, synthetic residues included. It's experimentally validated, which matters since most generative protein design quietly assumes the canonical alphabet is the whole alphabet.

original_title: 68 Ga-Labeled Dimeric Cyclic Peptide for Nectin-4–Targeted PET Imaging: From Preclinical Evaluation to First-in-Human Imaging in Breast Cancer
title: First human images from a Nectin-4 PET tracer
blurb: A dimeric Ga-68 cyclic peptide targeting Nectin-4, carried from preclinical testing into first-in-human PET scans in breast cancer. Nectin-4 is already an antibody-drug conjugate target, so a working tracer doubles as a way to pick who'd actually benefit from that drug.

original_title: (68)Ga-Labeled Dimeric Cyclic Peptide for Nectin-4-Targeted PET Imaging: From Preclinical Evaluation to First-in-Human Imaging in Breast Cancer.
title: A cyclic peptide dimer gets its first human Nectin-4 scan
blurb: The same translational arc: a preclinical Ga-68 dimeric cyclic peptide against Nectin-4 taken through to first-in-human PET imaging in breast cancer. Dimerizing the peptide looks like the design choice that gave it the affinity and pharmacokinetics to clear preclinical work and reach a patient scan.

original_title: On-DNA Synthesis of Arylhydrazones via Aryl Diazonium-Mediated Diazenylation
title: Building arylhydrazones directly on DNA-encoded libraries
blurb: In-situ generation of aryl diazonium intermediates on DNA conjugates, then coupling to active methylene compounds, gets arylhydrazones onto DNA-encoded library beads with broad substrate scope and good conversions on both coupling partners. Mostly useful if you're already running a DEL and want hydrazone pharmacophores in the mix.

original_title: Designing rhodamine-binding proteins from scratch
title: Designing a protein that grips rhodamine, starting from nothing
blurb: De novo designed proteins built specifically to bind the rhodamine dye, rather than repurposing an existing binder. A clean demonstration that small-molecule binding pockets, not just folds, are now something you can design to order.

original_title: Selective Ligand Replacement Leads to Carbene Complexes as Catalysts in Proteins
title: Swapping bipyridyl for carbene ligands on an artificial metalloenzyme
blurb: Follow-up to their Ru(II) piano-stool/bipyridyl transfer-hydrogenase artificial metalloenzyme, now trying pyridyl-NHC carbene ligands on the same Ru(arene) scaffold delivered into a naive protein. The ligand swap is the whole experiment, since carbenes bind the metal differently than bipyridyl, exactly the kind of knob you'd want the protein scaffold to tune.

original_title: Dehydrogenative Aminooxygenation of Cyclopropylamides Enabled by Cooperative Electrocatalysis
title: Cooperative electrocatalysis turns cyclopropylamides into oxazines
blurb: An electrochemical [3+3] annulation using amides, carbamates, and ureas as both nitrogen and oxygen sources, building 1,3-oxazines from cyclopropylamides with full regiocontrol. Billed as atom-economic and scalable at higher concentrations, and it reportedly handles late-stage substrates too, which is usually where these methods quietly fall apart.

original_title: Control of Helix Screw‐Sense Preference in Dynamic Foldamers of meso Symmetry Built From Chiral Monomeric Units
title: Getting meso foldamers to pick a handedness without losing their symmetry
blurb: Meso oligoureas normally need symmetric meso-cyclohexanediamine units to do their reversible helix-inversion trick, which caps how much the sequence can vary. Building meso and near-meso oligoureas from chiral monomers instead keeps that behavior while opening up sequence space, and desymmetrizing the terminal groups turns out to bias which screw-sense wins.

original_title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
title: Turning ethane and propane into chiral building blocks
blurb: HAT photocatalysis paired with a chiral nickel catalyst threads gaseous alkanes, ethane, propane, isobutane, into a three-component alkene dicarbofunctionalization, landing chiral α-aryl carbonyls with up to 20:1 regioselectivity and 99:1 er. Gaseous alkanes are usually too inert and too indifferent to stereochemistry to bother with, so getting both regio- and enantiocontrol out of them in one step is the actual trick.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Asymmetric Metal-Templated Synthesis of Congested Proline Derivatives via [3 + 2] Cycloaddition Reaction
title: Building proline's most congested stereocenters with a silver cycloaddition
blurb: An Ag(I)-catalyzed [3+2] cycloaddition stitches a chiral dehydroalanine Ni(II) complex onto various α-imino esters, assembling a pyrrolidine core with three stereocenters, two of them quaternary. Strip the nickel off with acid afterward and what's left is an enantiopure proline with an extra amino acid fragment hanging off it, a scaffold most routes would need a lot more steps to reach.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Chemo- and Enantioselective Radical 1,2-Carbosulfenylation of Diverse Alkenes with Broad Radical and Sulfur Compatibility
title: Copper radical chemistry finally gets a ligand toolbox for carbosulfenylation
blurb: Enantioselective carbosulfenylation of alkenes with alkyl halides is an old idea with a bad track record, since side reactions usually beat out stereocontrol. The fix is a tunable library of anionic N,N,N(P) ligands on copper that reportedly handles a wide range of both radical and sulfur partners, which is exactly the part that usually breaks this reaction.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
title: A photocatalyst that turns into a stronger reductant on command
blurb: CBZ6 is a carbazole photocatalyst that does double duty: under visible light it runs as the usual neutral photoredox catalyst, but it can also pick up an electron to form a Birch-type anion and flip into a sharply more reducing species. One catalyst covering both jobs instead of keeping a separate, harsher reductant around for the hard substrates.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
